strengths: Locals treat the late store as a tool, not nightlife—this will read as true to Japanese readers.
The dual feeling (I use it at 1 a.m. / I would not want my child on that shift) is a real neighborhood conversation, not tourism copy.
Loungewear, underwear-after-laundry, overtime bento: unremarkable scenes, correctly framed as unremarkable.

issues.location: How Japanese People Use the Night Store — weather/transport instrument
issues.problem: “Weather and transport instrument” is editor language. Locals would say they buy an umbrella or wait after missing a train.
issues.suggestion: Describe the errands (umbrella, stand-and-eat, decide on a taxi) without the instrument metaphor.

issues.location: How Japanese People Use the Night Store — fever medicine / 3 a.m. children’s medicine
issues.problem: A parent buying children’s medicine at a konbini is possible but not the default local pattern; drugstores carry that role more often.
issues.suggestion: Keep the quiet parent errand; switch the product to something konbini actually hold at 3 a.m., or hedge OTC.
